transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 16:30 PST | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Victor Lopez (Peregrine - Head of Platform), Aisha Kumar (Procurement), Ben Torres (Security), Clara Nguyen (Legal), Evan (SRE)

-- Auto-summary (auto-generated) --
Maya: quick overview of platform and what we'll need to close procurement & legal.

00:00 Maya Chen: Okay hi everyone thanks for making time, we'll run head-first but feel free to interrupt. I'm Maya, AE on the account and with me is Samir our solution engineer.
00:12 Victor Lopez: Hey thanks Maya, Victor here. We just wrapped an internal triage so apologies if we have some folks jumping in late.
00:20 Aisha Kumar: Hi all I'm Aisha from procurement, we want to understand the path to signing, pricing buckets, and any special escrow or contract triggers.
00:31 Samir Patel: Great — quick note, we'll cover MSA/DPA risk points, SLA expectations, KMS/HSM and SSO, and then run through a short pilot plan for benchmarks.
00:43 Ben Torres: For security I'll flag upfront we need KMS integration that supports our AWS KMS-derived HSM and we require audit logs with tenant-level retention, also data residency constraints for EU customers.
00:57 Maya Chen: That's helpful Ben. On the MSA side we've seen two common asks: limited liability cap and data processing addendum clarifications on controller/processor language.
01:12 Clara Nguyen: From legal, we need to verify sub-processor lists, the DPA termination language, and whether Redwood supports e-discovery requests.
01:24 Samir Patel: On the technical side, Peregrine, do you plan to use Hosted API or Dedicated capacity or private VPC?
01:33 Victor Lopez: We're evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput for our chat assistants, but open to a private deployment if the DPA & KMS terms are a blocker.
01:42 Maya Chen: Good, that maps to different pricing and SLA tiers. For Dedicated we can provide throughput SLOs, and for Private we offer a customer-managed control plane w/ optional on-prem packaging.
01:56 Evan (SRE): Quick Q on latency — what's realistic for 2k token context p95 on a dedicated pool?
02:05 Samir Patel: Roughly 200-300ms p95 for a generative workload on our M60 equivalent profiles at steady-state, though that depends on your batching and sequence distribution — we'll put exact numbers in the pilot runbook.
02:19 Ben Torres: Are those numbers for quantized models or fp16? We need to understand accuracy vs quantization tradeoffs.
02:27 Samir Patel: Good point — those were quantized INT8-flow estimates. If you need fp16 for higher fidelity, p95 will increase ~30-40% and cost will go up accordingly.
02:39 Aisha Kumar: From procurement, how do you handle committed vs on-demand pricing? We usually need committed tiers for budget predictability.
02:47 Maya Chen: We have reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated with monthly/annual commits. Commit discounts scale with term and reserved GPU count. We'll send a pricing matrix after the call.
02:57 Victor Lopez: And what about overage billing and burst capacity?
03:03 Maya Chen: Burst is configurable, and overage rates are in the same matrix. We can also set hard caps per-route to avoid billing surprises.

-- 10m mark --
10:01 Clara Nguyen: On MSA redlines, we will probably push back on indemnity and liability cap. Also need to confirm jurisdiction and mutual confidentiality obligations.
10:12 Maya Chen: Noted. Historically we see three levels: standard MSA, enterprise MSA with tailored redlines, and an addendum for highly regulated customers. We can map your clauses to those tiers.
10:26 Clara Nguyen: Also about DPA — data export and sub-processor notices need a 30-day notification window.
10:35 Samir Patel: From a security perspective, our platform supports per-customer encryption keys via BYOK integrations for Dedicated/Private. We use envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS. Occasionally the automatic logging labels keys as K-V cash in the transcript (laughs) — sorry that's me, K-V cache, not K-V cash.
10:57 Ben Torres: (laughs) I did see a reference to K-V cache earlier in the docs, yes KV cache is fine. Does Redwood support key rotation without disrupting in-flight sessions?
11:08 Samir Patel: Yes, key rotation is supported with a double-write model for a brief period; we have docs on rotation choreography. We'll attach the KMS playbook.

-- 20m mark --
20:05 Aisha Kumar: Procurement needs an approval timeline. If we get the pricing matrix and legal redlines this week can we make a decision before end of month? Our next procurement committee is 12/21.
20:16 Maya Chen: That's tight but doable. We'll aim to have materials by 12/18 to give you time for review.
20:22 Victor Lopez: On pilot scope — we'd want to test three flows: chat assistants with 2k context, embedding generation for search, and a reranker for QA. We want latency p95, token cost, and regression check per flow.
20:39 Samir Patel: Perfect, we'll define sample prompts, dataset slices, and run both hosted and dedicated configs so you can compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
20:50 Evan (SRE): Can we run the pilot in our EU region please — need to validate egress and residency?
20:56 Samir Patel: Yes, we can route to an EU-dedicated pool. We'll note region in the runbook and include egress accounting.

-- 30m mark --
30:10 Maya Chen: Legal question from Clara — do you require an escrow clause for model weights or is a certification and reproducible artifact sufficient?
30:22 Clara Nguyen: For us it's less about weights and more about continuity of service. If a vendor disappears we need a path to continuity — escrow or a contractual migration workflow.
30:33 Maya Chen: Understood, we can propose a business continuity addendum and provide our standard third-party escrow options.
30:40 Ben Torres: Also need SOC 2 type II report and ISO certification list.
30:45 Maya Chen: We'll attach the security pack with SOC 2, ISO summary, penetration test cadence, and prior audit notes.

-- 38m mark --
38:02 Aisha Kumar: On the commercial side, what does the approval chain look like — do you need an order form signed first or can we sign the MSA conditioned on pricing?
38:13 Maya Chen: We typically sign the MSA and then an order form that attaches pricing and committed capacity. We can include conditional attachments if needed for procurement timelines.
38:25 Victor Lopez: For SLAs, we need p99 availability SLO and a latency objective for high-tier routes — is that something you offer in Enterprise?
38:36 Samir Patel: Yes, enterprise tier includes p99 availability with credit-based remedies and dedicated routing. For latency SLOs we publish expected p95 based on model profile; contractual p99 latency is harder but we can build route prioritization and escalation paths.
38:52 Clara Nguyen: What about termination assistance — will Redwood provide data export and runbooks if we end the contract?
38:58 Maya Chen: We include exit assistance and data extraction APIs; scope and retention windows are in the DPA. We'll flag the DPA excerpt for export timelines.

-- 44m mark --
44:07 Ben Torres: One more quick technical note — do you support private networking peering and fine-grained RBAC? We need least-priv access for service accounts.
44:18 Samir Patel: Yes, VPC peering and customer-managed subnets are supported for Private/Dedicated. RBAC can be integrated with your SAML/SCIM provider and mapped to token scopes.
44:31 Evan (SRE): If we do private, what OS/network changes are needed on our side?
44:36 Samir Patel: Minimal — you need route tables and a peering endpoint; our ops team will provide a checklist. For on-prem we have an installer but that is heavier.

-- 49m mark --
49:05 Maya Chen: Okay to recap: Redwood to send pricing matrix, security pack, KMS playbook, and a pilot runbook. Peregrine legal to send top redlines. Procurement to confirm 12/21 committee. Pilot kickoff targeted week of 12/21.
49:26 Aisha Kumar: Sounds good, will flag internally and expect materials.
49:32 Clara Nguyen: We'll try to get redlines in by 12/22 but if anything critical comes up we'll call it out sooner.
49:40 Maya Chen: Great. Ben or Victor anything else for security or SRE?
49:45 Ben Torres: No, that's it — just please include the audit retention options.
49:50 Victor Lopez: All good, thanks everyone.
49:55 Maya Chen: Thank you all, we'll follow up via email and set the pilot calendar invite. Bye.
50:02 End of recording.

Notes about transcription: small imperfections (some product names transcribed as Redwood Inference variants or Redwood-verified got shortened). Some filler words removed for readability but many disfluencies preserved.
